passage: On the school trip bus in Lisbon, Paulo's head jerked sideways and he made a small hooting sound. Two boys in the seat ahead turned round and stared. Then one of them jerked his own head and hooted, and they both laughed. Paulo looked out of the window. His throat felt tight. He wished he could make himself small enough to disappear. Liam, sitting beside him, didn't turn round to the boys, and he didn't whisper "ignore them." He just kept holding out the packet of crisps. "Which dinosaur are we seeing first? I vote the big one." When they got off, the teacher had a quiet word with the two boys. Liam walked beside Paulo into the museum, still talking about teeth.

qa.q: What did Liam keep holding out to Paulo?
How did Paulo feel when the boys copied him, and what shows it?
qa.a: He felt hurt and embarrassed; he looked out of the window with a tight throat, wishing he could disappear.

qa.q: Which choice by Liam helped Paulo most, and why?
qa.a: He simply carried on as normal, sharing crisps and chatting about dinosaurs, so Paulo felt ordinary, not like a problem.

qa.q: How might the two boys see Paulo after the teacher's quiet word?
qa.a: They may realise the movements and sounds are not a joke or a choice, and stop copying him.

grounding: It shows a child with tics hurt by stares and mimicking, with a teacher stopping the mocking and a seatmate who carries on as normal.

passage: During silent reading, Pradeep grunted twice, loudly. Half the class spun round. Someone at the back grunted back, and giggles spread. Pradeep gripped his book so hard the page tore. His eyes stung. He had been trying to hold it in for ten whole minutes. Hafsa Ma'am closed her book. Her voice was calm but firm. "Eyes on your own pages. Pradeep has tics. They're sounds and movements his body makes that he doesn't choose, the way you don't choose a hiccup. Copying them is unkind, and it stops now." The room went quiet. Then Nivedita, next to Pradeep, slid her bookmark over so he could fix the torn page, and went on reading. At lunch Pradeep sat with her, and nobody grunted.

qa.q: What did Nivedita slide over to Pradeep?
qa.a: Her bookmark, so he could fix the torn page.

qa.q: What does Pradeep gripping his book so hard that the page tore show?
qa.a: It shows how hurt and tense he felt when the class laughed, after trying to hold in the sounds for ten minutes.

qa.q: What did Hafsa Ma'am's brief explanation change in the room?
qa.a: It made clear the tics weren't a choice and stopped the mocking, so the room went quiet.

qa.q: How does Nivedita's way of reacting differ from the back row?
qa.a: She simply helped with the torn page and carried on reading, treating Pradeep normally instead of laughing.

grounding: It shows a child with tics hurt by stares and mimicking, a teacher who briefly explains it is not a choice and stops the mocking, and a classmate who carries on normally.
